headline: Back-to-back long aerobic days close out a +16% volume block while easy-run cardiac drift continues to trend downward — aerobic efficiency is moving in the right direction.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your aerobic system is responding. Easy-run heart rate has dropped meaningfully compared to the prior block at comparable paces, which is a concrete signal that the training load is converting to fitness rather than just accumulating fatigue. The 20-week running streak — now matching your personal best — is the structural foundation behind that, and yesterday's 18 km following Thursday's long effort shows your back-to-back durability is in good shape.

The volume step-up this block is meaningful but not aggressive, and the pacing across your recent easy days looks appropriate for absorbing it. Your threshold data point from earlier this week places your lactate threshold in genuinely strong territory — that figure sits well above your marathon PB pace, which confirms the endurance base is currently supporting faster-end capacity, not just easy-zone volume.

Strength work dropped slightly against the prior block. It's not alarming at this volume level, but worth keeping an eye on across the next few weeks — the hybrid profile depends on both sides of the equation staying consistent.
watch_items: Watch whether the easy-run HR trend continues downward, or whether it flattens as weekly load stays elevated — a plateau here would suggest the body is absorbing rather than adapting.
Monitor how quickly you recover between longer efforts; back-to-back durability is a strength right now, but stacking more of them as volume grows warrants attention.
Track whether strength session frequency recovers to prior-block levels — a second consecutive lower week would be worth addressing deliberately.
Notice whether threshold pace holds or improves on the next comparable effort — one data point is promising, but the trend matters more.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 145 km vs 125 km prior block (+16%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
